title: वर्तमान भोजपुरमा गोर्खाली आक्रमण {Gorkhali invasion of present-day Bhojpur}
nepali: नेपाल एकीकरण भनौ या गोर्खा राज्य विस्तार अभियान, भन्दा धेरै अघिदेखि नै यस भोजपुर माझ किरात क्षेत्रभित्र किरात राईहरू बसोवास गर्दै आएका र यस क्षेत्रको राजनीतिक, आर्थिक पक्षमा उनीहरूको महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहँदै आएको कुरा विभिन्न प्रकाशित साहित्य,लेख रचनाहरूमा उल्लेख भएको छ । मुकुन्द सेनको राज्य विस्तारको क्रममा यो माझ किरात भोजपुर पनि सेन राज्यभित्र रहन गयो । सेन राज्यभित्र यो माझ किरात भोजपुर रहेता पनि यहाँको हर्ताकर्ता वा शासन प्रणालीमा यहाँ कै किरात राईहरूको भूमिका रहेको थियो । सेन शासन कालमा पहाड तिरको शासन सञ्चालनको लागि प्रमुख केन्द्र (राजधानी) चौदण्डीमा रहेको थियो । त्यहीँ रहेर पहाडतिरको प्रशासन सञ्चालन हुन्थ्यो । प्रशासन सञ्चालनको क्रममा किरात राईहरूको बढी भूमिका रहेको हुनाले सेन शासन कालमै यो भूमिमा प्रवेश गरेका गैर किरातहरू सन्तुष्ट थिएनन् । जसरी भए पनि यो राज्यमा आफ्नो भूमिका बढी रहोस् भन्ने गैरकिरातहरूको चाहना रहेको थियो । त्यसका लागि सेन राजालाई हटाउन अनिवार्य थियो । विकल्प खोज्दै जाँदा गोर्खाली राजा पृथ्वी नारायण शाहले गोर्खा राज्य विस्तार गर्दै काठमाडौं उपत्यका कब्जा गरी नुवाकोटमा बसिरहेका समयमा यस राज्य अन्तरगत पर्ने खार्पाका धनाढ्य हरिनन्दन पोखरेल र चौदण्डीका कर्मचारी स्वरूपसिंह कार्कीले नुवाकोट गई पृथ्वीनरायण शाहलाई भेटी माझ किरातमाथि हमला गरी कब्जा गर्न सुझाव दिए । सोही अनुसार गोर्खाली सेनाहरूलाई गैर किरातहरूको भरपुर सहयोगले यस भोजपुर माझ किरातमा हमला गराई बि.सं.१८३० मा गोर्खा राज्यमा भनौ वा नेपाल एकीकरणमा यो समाहित हुन गयो ।
american_english: Whether we call it the unification of Nepal or the Gorkhali state expansion campaign, various published literature and writings mention that long before this the Kirat Rais had been living in this Majh Kirat Bhojpur area within the Kirat region and had been playing an important role in the political and economic aspects of this region. In the course of Mukunda Sen's state expansion, this Majh Kirat Bhojpur also came to be within the Sen kingdom. Although this Majh Kirat Bhojpur remained within the Sen kingdom, the leadership or administration here was in the hands of the local Kirat Rais. During the Sen rule, the main center (capital) for governing the hill region was at Chaudandi. The administration of the hill region was carried out from there. Because the Kirat Rais had a greater role in the administration, the non-Kirats who had entered this land during the Sen period were not satisfied. The non-Kirats wished that their role in this state would be greater, by whatever means. For that, removing the Sen king was essential. While searching for an alternative, when Gorkhali king Prithvi Narayan Shah, expanding the Gorkha state, captured the Kathmandu Valley and was staying at Nuwakot, the wealthy Harinandan Pokharel of Kharpak, which fell under this state, and the employee Swarupsingh Karki of Chaudandi went to Nuwakot, met Prithvi Narayan Shah, and advised him to attack and capture Majh Kirat. Accordingly, with ample support from the non-Kirats, the Gorkhali forces were made to attack this Majh Kirat Bhojpur, and in B.S. 1830 it was incorporated into the Gorkha state, or rather into the unification of Nepal.

informal_english: Whether you call it Nepal's unification or the Gorkha state expansion push, the published stuff says the Kirat Rais had been living in this Majh Kirat Bhojpur patch of the Kirat region for ages before any of that, and were big players in the area's politics and economy. When Mukunda Sen expanded his state, this Majh Kirat Bhojpur ended up inside the Sen kingdom. Even so, the locals, the Kirat Rais, were the ones actually running things. Under the Sen mob, the main hub (capital) for running the hills was Chaudandi, and administration was handled from there. Because the Kirat Rais had such a big say, the non-Kirats who'd moved in during Sen times weren't happy about it; they wanted more of a role for themselves, no matter what it took, and that meant getting rid of the Sen king. So while looking for options, when Gorkhali king Prithvi Narayan Shah had grabbed the Kathmandu Valley and was holed up in Nuwakot, Harinandan Pokharel, a wealthy bloke from Kharpak, and Swarupsingh Karki, an official from Chaudandi, went to Nuwakot, met the king, and told him to attack and take Majh Kirat. Following their advice, and with heavy backing from the non-Kirats, the Gorkhali forces hit Majh Kirat Bhojpur, and by B.S. 1830 the place was folded into the Gorkha state, or, if you like, into the unification of Nepal.
